items.headline: Captain James Rodríguez leads experience
items.body: <cite index="2-1,2-2">James Rodríguez, who won the Golden Boot at the 2014 World Cup, is Colombia's captain; the 34-year-old recently switched to Minnesota United in the MLS</cite>. <cite index="2-3">Midfielder Richard Ríos is another key player to watch, having impressed for Jose Mourinho's Benfica this season</cite>.

items.headline: Star forward in career-best form
items.body: <cite index="5-12,5-13">Luis Díaz arrives in arguably the form of his career, having moved from Liverpool to Bayern Munich last summer and lifted the Bundesliga in his maiden campaign</cite>. <cite index="5-14">Díaz leads Colombia with 21 international goals from 72 appearances</cite>.

items.headline: Defensive backbone anchored by Palace duo
items.body: <cite index="5-16">Crystal Palace duo Daniel Muñoz and Jefferson Lerma anchor the right flank and midfield respectively</cite>. <cite index="5-17">Galatasaray's Davinson Sánchez and Bologna's Jhon Lucumí form a settled centre-back pairing, with Yerry Mina providing experienced cover</cite>.

metadata.defenders: Daniel Muñoz, Davinson Sánchez, Jhon Lucumí, Yerry Mina

items.headline: No major squad injuries reported
items.body: Colombia's full 26-man squad completed World Cup preparations without reported fitness concerns. All key players are available for tournament selection, with squad announced in late May ahead of final friendlies.

items.headline: Strong pre-tournament momentum secured
items.body: <cite index="13-1">Colombia's previous match was against Jordan in International Friendly Games, with the match ending 2-0 in Colombia's favor</cite>. <cite index="15-9">Jhon Arias was the star of the match, scoring both goals as Colombia controlled most of the action and closed their preparations with a convincing victory</cite>.

items.headline: Historic unbeaten run set tone for tournament
items.body: <cite index="3-25">Under Lorenzo's stewardship Colombia has guided them to wins over Germany, Brazil, Spain and Uruguay, as well as a 28-match unbeaten run</cite>. <cite index="3-26">They reached the final of the 2024 Copa America, only losing to Argentina in extra-time</cite>.

items.headline: Coach Lorenzo rebuilds Colombia project
items.body: <cite index="11-6,11-7">After Reinaldo Rueda's failure to qualify for Qatar, the Colombian Football Federation turned to Néstor Lorenzo as his replacement in 2022, and the 60-year-old responded by immediately steering the national team back on course and securing qualification for the 2026 tournament</cite>.

items.headline: Finished third in CONMEBOL qualifying
items.body: <cite index="5-2,5-3">Los Cafeteros sealed their place by finishing third in CONMEBOL qualifying with 28 points and edged Uruguay and Brazil on goal difference</cite>. <cite index="11-20">Colombia's success was built largely on their attacking prowess, as they scored 28 goals, the second-most among the qualified South American teams, behind only Argentina</cite>.

items.headline: Group K draw includes Portugal challenge
items.body: <cite index="5-23,5-24">Group K pits Los Cafeteros against tournament debutants Uzbekistan, DR Congo and Portugal, with the closing fixture against Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal in Miami potentially deciding the group winners</cite>.

items.headline: Uzbekistan opener in Mexico City
items.body: <cite index="15-4">Matchday 1: June 17, Uzbekistan vs Colombia, Mexico City, Estadio Azteca</cite>. Colombia face debutants Uzbekistan in their group-stage opener to begin their World Cup campaign.

items.headline: DR Congo matchday in Guadalajara
items.body: <cite index="15-4">Matchday 2: June 23, Colombia vs Congo, Guadalajara, Estadio Akron</cite>. Colombia play their second group fixture against DR Congo at a neutral venue in Mexico.

items.headline: Portugal finale in Miami
items.body: <cite index="15-4">Matchday 3: June 27, Colombia vs Portugal, Miami, Hard Rock Stadium</cite>. Colombia face Cristiano Ronaldo's Portugal in their final group match, with potential knockout implications.

items.headline: Attacking prowess is primary threat
items.body: <cite index="1-31">Spearheaded by Bayern Munich star Luis Diaz, Los Cafeteros have enough attacking firepower to trouble any team in the world</cite>. <cite index="11-21">Defensively, however, there was room for improvement, with 18 goals conceded, the most among the top-six finishers in qualifying</cite>.

items.headline: James Rodríguez role still critical despite age
items.body: <cite index="1-38">James Rodriguez may not be in his prime anymore, but his country will still be relying on him to lead by example and come up with a few more moments of magic in what is likely his last World Cup</cite>. Age and experience define his contribution as senior figure.

items.headline: Contenders for knockout advancement
items.body: <cite index="3-16">Los Cafeteros were one of four teams from CONMEBOL to qualify and will appear at World Cup 2026 with one of the most intriguing squads at the tournament, which has a mix of experience and breakthrough talent</cite>. Colombia are positioned as strong group contenders with capability to challenge elite teams.
